data.narrative:
Critical Loop, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Bala Ramamurthy, has raised $49M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies in the climate and energy sector—1 public and 8 private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. The stage-progression approach, which uses total capital raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A to next-stage progression, yields an implied valuation of $98M. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables; while eight peers operate in Climate & Energy, none met the filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comps), and using an all-sector median would introduce material distortion.

The triangulation, constrained to a single methodology, supports a valuation range of $83M (low) to $113M (high), with a median of $98M. This range reflects the inherent uncertainty of relying on a single method and the scarcity of tightly comparable Series A stage data within the climate and energy sector. Key uncertainties include the degree to which stage-based step-ups apply to this particular subsector and the absence of direct peer benchmarking to validate the 2.0x multiplier against Critical Loop's specific risk and growth profile.
